report.incidentSummary: Starting at 11:20:04 IST (05:50:04 UTC) on 2026-10-07, assistant-orchestrator began receiving HTTP 429 Too Many Requests errors ('quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000') from external llm-provider. The orchestrator's exponential backoff retry mechanism (retrying up to 3 times with 2-8 second delays) caused conversation p95 latencies to surge from ~6.2 seconds to 24-26 seconds. Approximately 6% of conversations exhausted all 3 retry attempts and failed with the generic fallback message 'Something went wrong'.
report.rootCauseStatement: assistant-orchestrator's token consumption (consistently between 211k and 267k tokens/min) breached the external llm-provider's 200,000 tokens-per-minute (TPM) quota, which began being enforced at 05:50:04 UTC. Consecutive retries with exponential backoff on HTTP 429 responses accumulated 20+ seconds of latency per conversation, and conversations that exhausted all 3 retries failed with a fallback error.

hypotheses.cause: assistant-orchestrator breached the 200,000 tokens-per-minute quota on external llm-provider starting at 05:50:04 UTC, receiving HTTP 429 Too Many Requests. Successive retry attempts with exponential backoff (2-8 seconds per attempt) accumulated 20+ seconds of latency, and conversations exhausting all 3 retries (~6% of traffic) failed with the generic fallback error message.
hypotheses.rationale: Directly confirmed by metric spikes in llm_latency_p95_ms (rising from 5s to ~23s), rate_limited_count (spiking from 0 to ~70/min), and explicit 429 error messages from llm-provider specifying 'quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000'. Token usage prior to 05:50 UTC was 211k-267k tokens/min, exceeding the 200k limit.

hypotheses.cause: The knowledge index rebuild (CHG-48222) on indexing-pipeline consumed shared organization quota on llm-provider for document embeddings, causing aggregate token consumption to breach the 200,000 TPM limit at 05:50 UTC.
hypotheses.rationale: Service dependency checks confirm indexing-pipeline depends only on knowledge-index and message-queue, and knowledge-index has no downstream dependencies. Neither service connects to llm-provider, ruling out shared quota consumption.

hypotheses.cause: The knowledge index rebuild (CHG-48222) triggered high retrieval latencies on knowledge-index, causing assistant-orchestrator requests to delay or time out (similar to PIR-2003).
hypotheses.rationale: knowledge-index latency p95 peaked at only 369 ms, retrieval logs showed passage lookups completing in 53-390 ms, and the orchestrator's timeout to knowledge-index is configured to 800 ms with 0 retries. This cannot explain 20+ second delays.

inferences.statement: The 20+ second response time observed by users is spent almost entirely in llm-provider retries and backoff sleeps following HTTP 429 responses.
The failure of conversations with 'Something went wrong' represents the ~6% of requests that exhausted all 3 LLM call retry attempts due to persistent rate limiting.
The knowledge index rebuild (CHG-48222) did not contribute to llm-provider rate limiting because neither indexing-pipeline nor knowledge-index connects to llm-provider.

assumptions.statement: The external llm-provider enforced the 200,000 tokens-per-minute account quota beginning around 05:50:00 UTC, or assistant-orchestrator's rolling minute usage crossed the provider's token-bucket boundary at that time.

No deployments, configuration adjustments, or scheduled job changes occurred on assistant-orchestrator, indexing-pipeline, or job-scheduler during this window.

Outside the 05:00-06:00 UTC window, the only other change in the broader window up to 07:30 UTC was CHG-48511 on mandate-service at 06:37:45 UTC (feature flag rollout order_ticket_redesign from 10% to 25%).

Prior changes on 2026-10-06 included CHG-48471 (indexing-pipeline cache TTL raised), CHG-48480 (user-context-service release 1.6.0), CHG-48496 (assistant-orchestrator release 0.42.1), and CHG-48506 (indexing-pipeline max replicas raised to 16). None occurred on 2026-10-07.

A closely similar historical incident occurred on 2026-09-02 (PIR-2003, SEV3: 'Assistant slow while knowledge index rebuilt'). Its symptoms were assistant answers taking 8-10 s during an index rebuild, caused by the rebuild running on serving nodes and elevating search p95 to 2.5 s. Its resolution recorded that rebuilds now run on separate nodes.
